thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: prod-cluster-3 | kv-cache eviction rate spike (-> 72k/min). cont-batch tail latency > 95th. Alert: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/8234

Raj: paging — I'm oncall. looking.

Olivia: oncall handoff acknowledged. pulling logs and live metrics now. which customer is hitting heavy seqs?

IncidentBot: top noisy origin: api-key-*-enterprise (3 keys). error pattern: `kv_cache::evict` + `batch_alloc_fail` in logs.

Olivia: seeing repeated `OOM when allocating kv page` on contbatch-pod-7. suspect batch aggregation blew up. grabbing config for cont-batch service.

Olivia: config dump (prod) ->
```
max_batch_tokens: 1000000
max_num_seqs: 128
timeout_ms: 12000
prefix_cache_pages: 8192
```

Erin: whoa that's way higher than defaults. last rollout was an autosuggest tuning PR earlier today? @Raj any rollout note?

Raj: I approved a quick perf tweak earlier to reduce latency for a PLG test, but I thought we only changed `timeout_ms`. checking audit.

Raj: audit shows a config artifact from `eng-runtime/perf-tune-2026-03-10` set `max_batch_tokens=1000000` accidentally (units mismatch).

Olivia: ok root cause likely mis-tuned `max_batch_tokens` -> huge in-memory KV pages + eviction storm during paging. mitigation plan: 1) revert max_batch_tokens to 65536, 2) reduce max_num_seqs to 8, 3) deploy API-level defensive guard to reject >65k tokens, 4) roll restarts canary region.

Jake: thumbs on rollback. customers impacted?

Olivia: noticed 3 enterprise customers had high tail-latency (10-25s) for generation requests; no large 5xx count but timeouts/early-close from clients. We should notify CS.

Marta: I'll draft an incident update to customers. hold on until we confirm mitigation works.

Raj: executing hotfix patch to configmap now. command:
```bash
kubectl -n redwood-prod patch configmap contbatch-config -p '{"data":{"max_batch_tokens":"65536","max_num_seqs":"8","timeout_ms":"2000"}}'
```

Olivia: also applying gateway guard to reject huge token requests to avoid immediate re-trigger while pods restart:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://gateway.redwood.internal/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"max_tokens_per_request":65536}'
```

Raj: patched. starting canary restart for contbatch deployment in us-west-2:
```bash
kubectl -n redwood-prod rollout restart deploy/contbatch-svc --selector=region=us-west-2
```

Olivia: monitoring metrics: eviction rate trending down (72k -> 3k in 90s), p95 latency falling from 18s -> 3.4s for canary. no new OOM logs on restarted pods.

Erin: good. what's the expected impact on throughput? will this increase cost?

Olivia: small throughput reduction per GPU for extremely long sequences (>65k tokens) but those are rare. unit-cost impact negligible compared to outage risk.

Marta: customer update draft: "We identified a misconfiguration in our continuous-batching runtime that caused excessive cache pressure and degraded request latency for a small set of customers. We've rolled a hotfix and are observing recovery. We will follow up with postmortem and remediation steps." Thoughts?

Jake: fine. add ETA for full recovery and whether any data loss (no data loss).

Olivia: full recovery expected within 15-25m as restarts converge; no data loss; requests that timed out should be retried by clients.

Raj: canary looks healthy, rolling to remaining regions now (eu, apac) with 10s stagger.

IncidentBot: deployment events: contbatch-svc rollout succeeded (canary).

Olivia: after eu rollout p95 steady ~2.8s, eviction rate normal. customers reported latency normalizing.

Erin: thanks team. assign follow-ups: 1) revert perf-tune branch -> open PR to remove accidental `max_batch_tokens` override (Raj), 2) add CI lint to detect insane token values (Olivia), 3) postmortem writeup + timeline (Marta + Jake).

Raj: created PR https://git.internal/eng-runtime/PR-498 to revert.

Olivia: created issue #3321 for CI lint rule.

Marta: I'll own postmortem. ETA EOD. will include customer impact timeline and proposed guardrails + docs for config units.

Jake: I'll coordinate customer comms and follow-up with the three affected accounts.

Raj: handing off oncall to Olivia at 12:40 UTC — if anything degrades ping me.

Olivia: taking over oncall. monitoring for 1h then hand to next rotation.

Marta: adding post-incident action items: add saturating cap in runtime that refuses to allocate >128k total batch tokens; add metric alert for sudden kv-page alloc growth; document safe ranges for `max_batch_tokens`.

Erin: add note: consider defaulting to token-count budget computed from GPU memory via autotuner (longer-term).

Olivia: final status: mitigated, recovery confirmed, low customer impact window ~18 minutes, hotfix rolled, follow-ups assigned. closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
